entries.0a92ed93f06c79a6: It operates the Tokaido Shinkansen between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. In the railway business results of the company (the reporting company) for the fiscal year ended March 2026, operating distance was 552.6 km; passengers carried were 183,924 thousand (commuter 13,947 thousand; non-commuter 169,977 thousand); passenger-kilometers were 60,860 million, up 10.2% year on year; and passenger transport revenue was ¥1,479,380 million (commuter ¥16,174 million; non-commuter ¥1,463,205 million), up 11.1% year on year. The seat occupancy rate was 67.9%. Non-commuter revenue accounts for nearly 99% of the total, a structure supported by business and travel demand. Considering that more than 60 years have passed since its opening, the company is advancing earthquake countermeasures covering the entire line, including derailment and deviation prevention measures, and large-scale renovation work to maintain the soundness of civil engineering structures. It began services in premium class seats (private compartment type) and is preparing to introduce semi-private compartment type seats within fiscal 2027.

entries.153cfcdc997b6f0b: Its head office is located at Meieki Itchome 1-4, Nakamura-ku, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture. In April 1987, it is one of the 6 passenger railway companies established when the Japanese National Railways Act was abolished in accordance with the 8 JNR reform-related laws. It consists of 27 consolidated subsidiaries and 2 equity-method companies (in the 39th fiscal period), and the number of consolidated employees as of March 31, 2026 was 29,569 (the annual average number of temporary employees, 7,634, is shown separately). The breakdown is 19,273 in Transportation, 6,691 in Other, 2,937 in Distribution and 668 in Real Estate, and among temporary employees, Distribution has the most, at 5,713. The submitting company alone has 18,518 employees (average age 37.0, average years of service 16.3; 16.4 years when years of service at Japanese National Railways are included), comprising 18,402 in Transportation and 116 in Real Estate. The company has 4 labor unions: the Tokai Passenger Railway Labor Union (18,485 members), the National Railway Workers' Union Tokai Headquarters (83 members), the JR Tokai Labor Union (57 members) and the JR Central Labor Union (10 members). Research and development is promoted at its research facility in Komaki City, Aichi Prefecture, which opened in July 2002.

entries.36be310d852e8c49: The operating length of the company's railway business is 552.6 km for the Shinkansen, 1,418.2 km for conventional lines, and 1,970.8 km in total. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, passengers carried totaled 565,579 thousand (excluding duplicate passengers between the Shinkansen and conventional lines; commuter passes 264,032 thousand, other than commuter passes 301,547 thousand), and passenger-kilometers totaled 69,724 million (Shinkansen 60,860; conventional lines 8,864). Transport efficiency was a Shinkansen seat occupancy rate of 67.9% and a conventional line boarding efficiency of 30.9%. Overlapping with this are the department store and station stores at Nagoya Station, the rental of station buildings, hotels, travel and advertising, and the manufacture of railway vehicles. Capital expenditure for the fiscal year ended March 2026 totaled ¥609 billion (¥615.9 billion including amounts covered by construction cost contributions), broken down as follows: the Transportation Business, ¥571 billion at the company and ¥0.5 billion at consolidated subsidiaries; Real Estate Business, ¥20.7 billion; Distribution Business, ¥8.3 billion; and Other, ¥8.2 billion. Investment in the Transportation Business was used for ensuring safe and stable transport on the Tokaido Shinkansen and conventional lines, improving services, constructing the Chuo Shinkansen, and improving operational efficiency. Total research and development expenses included in operating expenses were ¥43 billion. The main items were running tests using the N700S confirmation test vehicle, advancing and streamlining inspection and maintenance, reducing costs for the construction, operation and maintenance of the superconducting Maglev, and refining practical technologies. For the superconducting Maglev, the company has spent a total of ¥170.6 billion from the fiscal year ended March 1991 to the fiscal year ended March 2026 as special contributions toward experimental infrastructure facilities and similar on the Yamanashi Maglev Test Line, and a total of ¥344 billion from the fiscal year ended March 2007 to the fiscal year ended March 2026 for extension to 42.8 km and equipment renewal. Separately from these, it has spent a total of ¥317 billion on the company's own superconducting Maglev technology development costs from its establishment to the fiscal year ended March 2026. In March 2026, the Superconducting Maglev Practical Technology Evaluation Committee of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism gave an evaluation that, because comprehensive verification of the technology development issues in the basic plan has been completed, technology development under the basic plan will end.

entries.59d0cb6c44d9c93a: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥830,167 million, up ¥127.3 billion (18.1%) from the previous fiscal year. Operating expenses were ¥1,176,000 million (up 4.2% year on year), below the rate of revenue growth. Profit by segment (operating profit) was ¥767,472 million in Transportation, ¥25,279 million in Real Estate, ¥24,460 million in Other, ¥15,822 million in Distribution and an adjustment of -¥2,867 million, with Transportation accounting for more than 9-tenths. Non-operating profit and loss improved by ¥4.2 billion compared with the previous fiscal year, and ordinary profit was ¥780,914 million (up 20.3% year on year) and net income attributable to owners of parent was ¥552,871 million (up 20.6%). Net assets at the end of the period increased by ¥478 billion from the end of the previous fiscal year to ¥5,136,600 million, and liabilities were ¥5,739,500 million. The balance of long-term debt at the end of the period was ¥4,768,400 million, of which the balance of long-term debt excluding long-term borrowings for the construction of the Chuo Shinkansen was ¥1,768,400 million, a decrease of ¥10.2 billion from the end of the previous fiscal year. For the construction of the Chuo Shinkansen, it took out long-term borrowings using the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program in fiscal 2016 and fiscal 2017, securing the funds needed for the time being. Cash flow from operating activities increased by ¥748.1 billion, cash flow from investing activities decreased by ¥621.4 billion and cash flow from financing activities decreased by ¥150.8 billion, and cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period were ¥370.5 billion. In this period, it raised ¥73.8 billion through long-term borrowings.

entries.97f6d9a4f90ff266: A reportable segment that operates the railway business on the Tokaido Shinkansen and conventional lines in the Tokai region, as well as the bus business and others. The company's railway business has operating distances of 552.6km for the Shinkansen and 1,418.2km for conventional lines, a total of 1,970.8km. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥1,641,663 million, accounting for 8 tenths of consolidated operating revenue, and segment profit (operating income) was ¥767,472 million, a scale that covers almost all of consolidated operating income. Segment assets were ¥10,003,296 million, the number of employees was 19,273, and capital expenditures were ¥571.0 billion for the company and ¥0.5 billion for consolidated subsidiaries. Regarding the Tokaido Shinkansen, the company explains that it completed transport for the Japan International Exposition 2025 (Osaka-Kansai Expo) and, in addition to the "Nozomi 12-train timetable", made use of a timetable that, since the March timetable revision, runs up to 13 "Nozomi" trains per hour in some time slots. It is advancing earthquake countermeasures, including the installation of derailment prevention guards along the entire line, and large-scale renovation work, and continues to introduce the N700S. On conventional lines, it completed the introduction of the 315 series commuter trains across all cars, and began one-man operation with 4-car 315 series trains equipped with a safety confirmation support device using cameras on the sides of the cars and image recognition technology. The main affiliated companies are the company and JR Tokai Bus Co., Ltd.

entries.f528ab433b0bb24b: The company positions the operation of high-speed railways linking the Tokyo metropolitan area, the Chukyo area and the Kinki area as its own mission. Passengers carried in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were 264,032 thousand on commuter passes and 301,547 thousand other than commuter passes, with a clear difference in character between the Shinkansen and conventional lines. Of the Shinkansen's passenger transport revenue of ¥1,479,380 million, non-commuter revenue accounted for ¥1,463,205 million, and demand is centered on business trips and travel. Conventional lines carried 395,252 thousand passengers, with passenger transport revenue of ¥106,000 million (of which commuter pass revenue was ¥32,433 million), and short-distance use for commuting and school travel is common. Some tickets are sold through other JR companies and their travel agencies, and the share of sales amounts in the company's passenger transport revenue is 15.3% for East Japan Railway Company (17.1% in the previous year) and 13.6% for West Japan Railway Company (14.5% in the previous year). For inbound foreign visitors, the company analyzed passenger trends and product usage by country and region, and expanded sales channels through cooperation with travel agencies. Because sales to external customers in Japan exceed 90% of total sales, region-specific information is not disclosed.
